### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/types`, touching **31** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via DuplicateRecordError (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via DuplicateRecordError (symbol, a top-level class), structuredCodeAnswer (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f44d55ea5b382c9f88086eafbee18ca5f506745a` — the merge of head `0b701b1551e4761e3e0c2a097f819c6f5e3014c1` into base `6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f44d55ea5b382c9f88086eafbee18ca5f506745a && git checkout f44d55ea5b382c9f88086eafbee18ca5f506745a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3 0b701b1551e4761e3e0c2a097f819c6f5e3014c1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3 && git merge --no-ff 0b701b1551e4761e3e0c2a097f819c6f5e3014c1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `af12b055c225e462e708648317284d819b2b1405`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts, packages/types/src/unique-violation.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts, packages/objectql/src/duplicate-record-error.ts + packages/rest/src/rest-duplicate-record-arm.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-duplicate-record-label-sentence.test.ts, packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.test.ts, packages/types/src/unique-violation.test.ts

### ① Derived judgments

- **Spec (hit).** `BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES` gains `duplicate_record`, `duplicate_record_field` and `duplicate_record_fields` in every platform locale (the every-locale-defines-every-key test). The English strings are byte-identical to the fixed text the classification answered before for a single field or none. These are additive catalog keys and a deployment can override them through `errors.duplicate_record*`. Nothing an author writes moves, so `Metadata-protocol: none` and `@objectstack/spec: patch` hold.
- **Types.** `uniqueViolationColumns(error)` returns columns only where every part is a plain column and at least two remain after the organization part is set aside, so it never overlaps `uniqueViolationField`. The jsdoc's "driver text is evidence, not a verdict" is honoured by the one caller.
- **Engine.** A composite key is named only when the reported columns match, as a set and with no duplicates, a `unique: 'global' | 'organization'` index the object declares, and every field has a real label (a translation or the declared `label`, never the API name). Otherwise it uses the nameless sentence. That keeps "a wrong field name is worse than none". `endUserMessage` is rendered through `renderOperationMessage` with the write context's `locale`/`translate`, the same ladder `DELETE_RESTRICTED` uses. Values never reach the sentence, which is pinned (`not.toContain(VALUE)`).
- **Wire.** `mapDataError` relays `endUserMessage` as `error` when present, else the old English. `code`, status `409` and the `field` key (one determinable column only) are unchanged. On a real better-sqlite3 driver, a composite conflict answers the labelled sentence in `en` and `zh-CN` with no `field` key.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` holds: new exports and catalog keys, and no input is refused. The `error` text now follows the writer's language. That changes the language of a human-facing field, not a contract member.
- nit N1: in English the composite list reads `the same “Tenant”, “Email”` (shared `field_label_list_separator`). "“Tenant” and “Email”" would read better. That's a catalog wording choice for later.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/types` and `@objectstack/objectql` with `Metadata-protocol: none` (AGENTS.md: `none` takes `patch`). Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Published schema package touched (`packages/spec/src/system/**`): catalog constant only, no zod schema.
- Same catalog family as #33290 (A2, packaged-set lock texts hand-coded in 11 languages). This PR shows the catalog route works for engine refusals too, which supports #33290's N1 follow-up.
- CI at this head when read (17:20Z): 16 success, 11 skipped, 36 in progress, none red. The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.

### ④ Design judgment

#33213 asks that a duplicate refusal read in the writer's language and say which combination collided. Composing at the producer (the engine, which holds the schema and the locale), and relaying in the classification (which holds neither), is the same split ruling C on #32440 set for refusal sentences. Matching driver columns against a declared index before naming anything turns driver text into a verdict only when the schema confirms it. Three keys chosen by how much can be named honestly is the smallest catalog that covers the cases. The design holds.
